memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But the Egyptian magicians did the same things by their secret arts, and Pharaoh's heart became hard; he would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the Lord had said." - Exodus 7:22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
There is something almost absurd here. Egypt has no drinkable water. Instead of asking Moses to remove the plague, Pharaoh's magicians produce more blood.

They could imitate the judgement. They could not reverse it. And their little demonstration gave Pharaoh just enough excuse to keep his heart hard.

Pride works exactly like this. It would rather match an opponent than admit a need. It would rather make the problem worse than accept help. How many marriages, friendships and churches have been damaged because someone needed to win rather than to be healed?

Notice the cost of Pharaoh's stubbornness — his own people suffered. Hard-hearted leaders rarely suffer alone.

The magicians could copy the plague, but they could not undo it. Only God can undo. That is the difference between every human system and the gospel: religion can imitate morality, philosophy can imitate wisdom, but only Christ can actually cleanse a heart.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where is my pride making a problem worse instead of asking for help?
2. Do I need to win an argument more than I need to be reconciled?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, humble me before my pride costs me more. Help me to seek healing rather than victory. Amen.
